https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/48408
## Motivation

LPM falls back to FCFS for long waiting queues to limit prefix matching and sorting costs. When reusable prefixes compete for a small KV pool, this can lose useful locality. This change offers a bounded window for cache-aware ordering while preserving the default behavior.

## Modifications

- Add `--lpm-window-size N` to the existing `lpm` policy. Default `0` preserves the current behavior, including large-queue fallback.
- With a positive window, match and stably reorder only the first N waiting requests. Leave the tail in place and bypass the large-queue fallback for this window.
- Retain admission-time matching because requests outside the window have not been matched. Retain the existing FCFS adjustment when prefix caching is disabled.
- Reject negative values and positive windows combined with another scheduling policy or priority scheduling.
- Add registered CPU tests for window boundaries, ties, tail preservation, the iterable-input/list-output contract, duplicate-prefix deferral, disabled caching, default fallback, CLI parsing and invalid configurations.
- Document empirical window selection and the tradeoff between cache locality, scheduler cost and cold-request waiting time. No experimental timers are added to production code.

The window bounds the requests considered for matching and sorting, not total scheduler work or maximum waiting time.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-forward or kernel changes. Earlier GPU validation compared the same 16 sequential requests across four policies and obtained matching outputs; this is an output regression check, not an accuracy benchmark.

The implementation is adapted to upstream `77c3bcbe2c28e1a6d1ad4121ee57231582d39bdc`, including the new iterable-input/list-output scheduling API. The GPU measurements below were collected on the earlier implementation based on `26fde018e53840238624f7810b69ca641531713c`; they have not been rerun on the rebased revision.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

45 runs: stock LPM and K=16/32/64/128, three scenarios, three repetitions. RTX 4090, Qwen3-4B, max-running-requests=32, output length 16, 512-request synthetic bursts, identical seed-11 inputs. Every trial restarts the server and follows the same initialization and cache warmup procedure. Execution order is randomized within each repeat. All 23,040 measured requests complete with zero retractions.

The constrained-cache workload has 384 hot requests across 12 shared-prefix groups and 128 cold requests, with 1040 input tokens per request. Percentages below average the changes relative to stock LPM within the same repetition.

| Window | Throughput (req/s) | Throughput change | Mean TTFT change | Cold p95 TTFT change | Cache reuse |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stock | 15.834 | — | — | — | 25.30% |
| 16 | 19.074 | +20.48% | -25.24% | -19.62% | 44.62% |
| 32 | 24.519 | +54.86% | -43.24% | -37.58% | 56.51% |
| 64 | 29.543 | +86.58% | -55.70% | -47.88% | 63.76% |
| 128 | 32.902 | +107.81% | -65.31% | -53.12% | 68.89% |

The KV pool above holds 8192 tokens. K128 has the best throughput among the tested candidates; its three runs span 32.759–33.111 req/s versus 29.106–29.818 for K64. This does not establish a global optimum or a plateau beyond 128.

Controls matter: with a 32768-token pool, throughput changes range from -1.04% to +0.76%, while cold mean TTFT increases by 6.35%, 14.07%, and 19.31% for K32/K64/K128. K128 cold p95 changes by -1.06% but cold p99 by +1.74%; the average-delay regression must not be hidden by the p95 result. In the no-reuse control, throughput changes range from -0.18% to +0.09%.

Keep the default at 0. For similar cache-constrained prefix-sharing bursts, try 128; start with 32 if you need a smaller scheduling budget and less cold-request delay, and measure your own workload. With sufficient cache or no reuse, these measurements do not justify enabling the option. This recommendation covers one model, one GPU and one input seed with three execution repetitions, not production traffic or all batch/output settings.

The CPU microbenchmark uses Python RadixCache, not the GPU server's Rust backend. At queue length 512 and input length 1024, median thread CPU times for K16/32/64/128 are 0.431/0.904/1.585/2.953 ms. This illustrates the cost trend but is not a CPU profile of the GPU-serving process.

## Validation

- 34 targeted tests passed on Linux against the rebased implementation: 11 new bounded-LPM tests and 23 existing scheduling, CLI metadata, argument-documentation and waiting-prefix-refresh tests.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed on the seven changed files; git diff --check passed.
- Full-repository pre-commit was attempted on macOS. Two unrelated Rust hooks could not pass: the gateway rustfmt hook requires rustup on PATH, and the Rust workspace uses Linux-only socket APIs. Formatter changes to unrelated files were discarded.
- Full Mintlify site validation has not run; argument-documentation coverage tests passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Run applicable pre-commit hooks on all changed files.
- [x] Add registered CPU unit tests using CustomTestCase.
- [x] Update argument and tuning documentation.
- [x] Report speed results, negative controls and the scope of output checks.
- [x] Follow the existing scheduler's interfaces and code style.

Full-project CI and multi-GPU TP, PD and external-cache backend validation remain outstanding. A single-GPU benchmark does not establish compatibility with all serving modes.

@@ -80,3 +80,14 @@ Data parallelism is better for throughput. When there is enough GPU memory, alwa
 - Try other quantization (e.g. FP8 quantization with `--quantization fp8`)
 - Try other parallelism strategies (e.g. [expert parallelism](https://lmsys.org/blog/2025-05-05-large-scale-ep/)) or DP attention for deepseek models (with `--attn-dp-size 8`).
 - If the workload has many shared prefixes, try `--schedule-policy lpm`. Here, `lpm` stands for longest prefix match. It reorders requests to encourage more cache hits but introduces more scheduling overhead.
+
+
+### Bounded LPM matching window
+
+With `--schedule-policy lpm --lpm-window-size 128`, only the first 128 waiting requests are matched and reordered on each scheduling pass. The remaining requests retain their order, and admission still performs the necessary prefix matching. This opt-in mode bypasses LPM's large-queue FCFS fallback. The default value, zero, preserves existing behavior.
+
+A bounded window can help when queued requests compete for a limited prefix cache. It can add overhead without useful reuse and delay cache-cold requests when cached requests are prioritized. It does not guarantee a maximum waiting time. Compare throughput and cold-request tail latency on your workload before enabling it. Priority scheduling is not supported with a positive window. Disabling prefix caching retains the existing FCFS fallback.
+
+For cache-constrained bursts with shared prefixes, try a window of 128 and measure throughput together with cold-request mean and tail latency. In a single-GPU RTX 4090 test with Qwen3-4B, 512 synthetic requests, an 8192-token KV pool, a running-request limit of 32, and 16 output tokens, 128 gave the highest throughput among windows of 16, 32, 64, and 128 across three repetitions of the same input seed. This is an empirical starting point for similar workloads, not a universal optimum.
+
+If you need a smaller scheduling budget or less impact on cold requests, start with 32 and compare it with 64 and 128. With a 32768-token pool, the same test showed little throughput change, while cold-request mean TTFT increased by about 6%, 14%, and 19% for those windows. Keep the default of 0 unless measurements on your workload justify enabling a window.

+import argparse
+import unittest
+from array import array
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_policy import (
+    CacheAgnosticPolicy,
+    CacheAwarePolicy,
+    SchedulePolicy,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixCache
+from sglang.srt.sampling.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def policy(k=0, name="lpm", disabled=False, priority=False):
+    cache = RadixCache.create_simulated()
+    cache.disable = disabled
+    return SchedulePolicy(name, cache, False, priority, False, lpm_window_size=k)
+
+
+class TestBoundedLPM(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_window_boundaries_and_stable_ties(self):
+        for k in (1, 16, 32, 64, 128):
+            for n in sorted({0, 1, k - 1, k, k + 1, 128, 129, 512}):
+                with self.subTest(k=k, n=n):
+                    p = policy(k)
+                    q = [
+                        SimpleNamespace(rid=str(i), num_matched_prefix_tokens=i % 3)
+                        for i in range(n)
+                    ]
+                    before = q.copy()
+                    with patch.object(
+                        p, "_compute_prefix_matches", return_value=set()
+                    ) as match:
+                        q = p.calc_priority(q)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        q[:k],
+                        sorted(before[:k], key=lambda r: -r.num_matched_prefix_tokens),
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(q[k:], before[k:])
+                    self.assertEqual(sorted(map(id, q)), sorted(map(id, before)))
+                    self.assertEqual(match.call_args.args[0], q[:k])
+                    self.assertFalse(p.waiting_queue_prefix_matched(q))
+
+    def test_input_iterable_is_not_reordered(self):
+        p = policy(2)
+        original = [
+            SimpleNamespace(rid=str(i), num_matched_prefix_tokens=i) for i in range(4)
+        ]
+        with patch.object(p, "_compute_prefix_matches", return_value=set()):
+            result = p.calc_priority(iter(original))
+        self.assertEqual([r.rid for r in original], ["0", "1", "2", "3"])
+        self.assertEqual([r.rid for r in result], ["1", "0", "2", "3"])
+
+    def test_default_fallback_and_other_policy(self):
+        p = policy()
+        self.assertEqual(p._determine_active_policy([None] * 128), CacheAwarePolicy.LPM)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            p._determine_active_policy([None] * 129), CacheAgnosticPolicy.FCFS
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            policy(name="hrrn")._determine_active_policy([None] * 129),
+            CacheAgnosticPolicy.FCFS,
+        )
+
+    def test_deprioritized_remains_inside_window(self):
+        p = policy(2)
+        q = [
+            SimpleNamespace(rid=str(i), num_matched_prefix_tokens=100 - i)
+            for i in range(4)
+        ]
+        with patch.object(p, "_compute_prefix_matches", return_value={"0"}):
+            q = p.calc_priority(q)
+        self.assertEqual([r.rid for r in q], ["1", "0", "2", "3"])
+
+    def test_disabled_cache_delegates_fcfs(self):
+        p = policy(32, disabled=True)
+        self.assertEqual(p.policy, CacheAgnosticPolicy.FCFS)
+        q = [SimpleNamespace(rid="a"), SimpleNamespace(rid="b")]
+        with (
+            patch.object(p, "_compute_prefix_matches") as match,
+            patch.object(p, "_touch_waiting_prefixes") as touch,
+        ):
+            q = p.calc_priority(q)
+            match.assert_not_called()
+            touch.assert_called_once()
+        self.assertEqual([r.rid for r in q], ["a", "b"])
+
+    def test_validation(self):
+        for k, name, priority in [
+            (-1, "lpm", False),
+            (32, "fcfs", False),
+            (32, "hrrn", False),
+            (32, "lpm", True),
+        ]:
+            with (
+                self.subTest(k=k, name=name, priority=priority),
+                self.assertRaises(ValueError),
+            ):
+                policy(k, name, priority=priority)
+
+    def test_server_args_reject_invalid_windows(self):
+        for kwargs, message in [
+            ({"lpm_window_size": -1}, "must be non-negative"),
+            ({"lpm_window_size": 32, "schedule_policy": "fcfs"}, "requires"),
+            (
+                {"lpm_window_size": 32, "enable_priority_scheduling": True},
+                "does not support priority scheduling",
+            ),
+        ]:
+            with self.subTest(kwargs=kwargs):
+                values = {"model_path": "dummy", "schedule_policy": "lpm", **kwargs}
+                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, message):
+                    ServerArgs(**values).check_server_args()
+
+    def test_cli(self):
+        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+        ServerArgs.add_cli_args(parser)
+        a = ServerArgs.from_cli_args(parser.parse_args(["--model", "dummy"]))
+        self.assertEqual(a.lpm_window_size, 0)
+        a = ServerArgs.from_cli_args(
+            parser.parse_args(
+                [
+                    "--model",
+                    "dummy",
+                    "--schedule-policy",
+                    "lpm",
+                    "--lpm-window-size",
+                    "64",
+                ]
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(a.lpm_window_size, 64)
+
+    def test_real_in_batch_matching_and_tail(self):
+        def req(i, tokens):
+            return Req(str(i), "", array("q", tokens), SamplingParams())
+
+        p = policy(2)
+        a = req(0, list(range(100)))
+        b = req(1, list(range(100)))
+        c = req(2, list(range(200, 300)))
+        p.calc_priority([a, b, c])
+        self.assertFalse(p.waiting_queue_prefix_matched([a, b, c]))
+        # A fully covered window follows ordinary LPM, including duplicate-prefix deferral.
+        qa = [
+            req(i, list(range(100)) if i < 2 else list(range(200, 300)))
+            for i in range(3)
+        ]
+        qb = [
+            req(i, list(range(100)) if i < 2 else list(range(200, 300)))
+            for i in range(3)
+        ]
+        qa = policy(64).calc_priority(qa)
+        qb = policy(0).calc_priority(qb)
+        self.assertEqual([r.rid for r in qa], [r.rid for r in qb])
+
+    def test_fast_match_tail_is_not_reported_as_matched(self):
+        p = policy(32)
+        with patch.object(
+            p.tree_cache, "supports_fast_match_prefix", return_value=True
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(p.waiting_queue_prefix_matched([None] * 129))
+
+    def test_matching_exception_propagates(self):
+        p = policy(32)
+        with patch.object(
+            p, "_compute_prefix_matches", side_effect=RuntimeError("expected")
+        ):
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "expected"):
+                p.calc_priority([])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

### 🟢 Approval recommended No active review issues remain for the opt-in bounded LPM scheduling change. **No open issues** 🎉
